title: Longest Slice Summing To K
statement:
Given an integer array nums (values may be negative) and a target k, return the length of the longest contiguous slice whose elements add up to exactly k.

Return 0 if no slice adds up to k.

examples.why: [2, -1, 3] sums to 4, but [-1, 3, -2, 4] also does and is longer. A shrinking window would stop at the shorter one, because negative numbers break the "sum only grows" assumption.
Every slice has a positive sum. An empty slice does not count.

hints: The sum of nums[i..j] is prefix[j + 1] − prefix[i]. What do you need to find for a fixed right end?
For right end j you want the earliest index i with prefix[i] = prefix[j + 1] − k. A hash map can answer that in O(1).
Store each prefix sum the first time you see it, never overwrite it, and seed the map with prefix 0 at index 0.

explain.intuition:
Negative numbers rule out a sliding window: growing the window can make the sum smaller, so you never know which way to move. Prefix sums still work. If prefix is the running total, the slice ending at j and starting after position i sums to k exactly when prefix[i] = prefix[j] − k.

To make that slice as long as possible, you want the earliest position with that prefix value. So remember only the first index at which each prefix sum appears. It is a lookup table keyed by running total, like caching the first timestamp each value was seen.
steps: Create a map first with first[0] = −1 (an empty prefix before index 0).
Walk j from left to right, adding nums[j] to sum.
If sum − k is in first, update best with j − first[sum − k].
If sum is not yet in first, set first[sum] = j.
pitfalls: Overwriting a prefix sum's index with a later one. That gives the shortest slice, not the longest.
Forgetting the seed first[0] = −1, which misses slices that start at index 0, like the whole array in the third example.
Using a shrinking window. It assumes all numbers are positive.

solutions.title: Every start, running sum
solutions.idea: Fix each start, extend the end one step at a time and keep a running sum.

solutions.title: Prefix sums + first-seen map
solutions.idea: For each running sum, look up the earliest index whose prefix is exactly k less.

followups: Count how many slices sum to k instead of finding the longest.
All numbers are positive now. Can you solve it in O(1) extra space?
lcTitle: Maximum Size Subarray Sum Equals k
